transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-06
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~65 minutes
Recording: auto

Summary (auto):
Kickoff for a POC to decide between Hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated reserved pools, or Private (VPC/on-prem) for Verdigris' inference needs. Focus areas: security & compliance, throughput/latency benchmarks, cost targets, and a 4-week pilot plan. Agreement to exchange security artifacts, traffic samples, and a benchmark harness.

Topics covered:
- Regulatory constraints (data residency, audit logs, KMS)
- Workload sizing: tokens per request, concurrency, QPS, burst patterns
- Success criteria: latency (p50/p95/p99), cost per 1k tokens, failover behavior, model parity
- Benchmarks & timeline: 2-week bench sprint + 2-week pilot + gating criteria
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency, cost, predictability, infra ops)

-- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, imperfect transcription):
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros from our side — I'm Maya, AE on the account, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer.
[00:07] Diego (Redwood SE): Hey all. I'll be driving the bench plan and the demo infra.
[00:12] Lena (Verdigris): Hey, Lena here — head of ML. Marcus is infra, Priya is on security, Tom is product.
[00:16] Marcus: Morning.
[00:18] Priya: Hi.
[00:20] Tom: Hi folks.
[00:22] Maya: Great. Objective for today is to scope a POC — decide which deployment pathway makes sense for you: the hosted Redwood API for rapid time-to-value, Redwood Dedicated for reserved capacity, or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulatory control. We'll capture success criteria, sizing, benchmarks, and a tentative timeline.
[00:40] Lena: High level constraints: we have PHI-ish telemetry data and some EU residency requirements. We need audit logs and a KMS/HSM-backed key management setup. SOC2 is a must, and our legal wants encryption in transit and at rest.
[00:55] Priya: Also SSO via SAML and RBAC across environments. We need per-tenant audit trails for a subset of users.
[01:05] Diego: Okay, that's consistent with other regulated customers. Hosted can work if we provide VPC peering and bring-your-own-key via KMS — though we need to double-check the KMS handshake. For strict residency or offline needs, Private (on-prem or VPC private control plane) is recommended. Dedicated is a middle ground: reserved GPU pools in a region, isolated and with network controls.
[01:30] Tom: From product: our acceptance criteria will be functional parity with our current internal models, <200ms p50 for short prompts, p95 under 400ms for most requests, and cost under our current inf infra baseline, roughly $X per 1k tokens — we'll share the exact baseline.
[01:50] Maya: Helpful. Can you give us an idea of your request shapes? tokens per request, typical and peak concurrency, and average QPS?
[02:05] Lena: Primarily two shapes: conversational chat messages (avg 300–800 tokens per request including context) and classification/rerank calls (10–60 tokens). Steady QPS is about 8–12, but peaks hit 120 for short bursts during biz spikes. Concurrency we expect up to 100 concurrent in early prod.
[02:30] Marcus: Also, some batch jobs at night that hit bulk embeddings, like 500k vectors per run, but that's offline and can be offloaded.
[02:44] Diego: Great — that helps. For benchmarking we should target three profiles: 1) short-latency chat path (300 tokens, concurrency 50), 2) mid-length chat (700 tokens, concurrency 20), and 3) small classification/rerank at high qps (50 tokens, concurrency 100). We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), and cost per 1M tokens.
[03:12] Marcus: Do you do KV cache / prefix cache across requests? We're worried about cold-start when users open long sessions.
[03:20] Diego: Yes, Redwood's runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching — though the behavior differs slightly across deployment modes. Hosted can share cache policy with regional affinity; Dedicated can be pinned per-customer; Private gives you full control but requires you to operate cache nodes. We'll benchmark with and without cache to show delta.
[03:40] Priya: For security review — we need network diagrams, where keys live, how audit logs are exported, retention policies. Is the private offering fully air-gapped if needed?
[03:53] Maya: Private on-prem can be deployed without egress, yes. For VPC Private, there is a control-plane connection, but logs and data can remain in-customer VPC. We will send the security pack.
[04:06] Lena: Timeline thoughts? We want quick answers — ideally a decision in 6 weeks.
[04:12] Maya: Our typical pilot structure: Week 0–1: kick off & artifacts exchanged; Week 1–2: benchmark sprint (configure harness, run tests across Hosted, Dedicated, Private variants as feasible); Week 3–4: production-like pilot on chosen mode and validation; then decision. That aligns with 4–6 weeks.
[04:30] Tom: Ok good. On the Dedicated side — how predictable is tail latency? Our SLAs are strict.
[04:36] Diego: Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools and SLO-backed latency tiers. Tail is more predictable because you're not contending with noisy neighbors. For p99 behavior we still need to look at sequence length variance and batching impact. We'll surface p99 and p999 in the benchmark.
[04:57] Lena: Cost tradeoffs? Initial thought is hosted is cheapest to start but cost per token scales; Dedicated has lower unit cost at high volume with commit; Private has ops overhead.
[05:12] Maya: Exactly. We'll provide a cost model spreadsheet: per-token hosted pricing, reserved commit options for Dedicated, plus estimated ops/infra cost for Private (license + infra + SRE). We'll model TCO over 12 months for the traffic traces you share.
[05:28] Marcus: We have to consider GPU types — some models run better on A100 vs H100 vs newer inference chips. Do you expose quantized model variants?
[05:38] Diego: We support quantized variants and kernel selection in runtime. During benching we'll test the same model family across different quantization levels and hardware where available, and note any quality regressions. We'll also test fallbacks in case a model variant isn't available in a region.
[05:58] Priya: Auditability: we need immutable logs, and the ability to subscribe to real time events for critical actions, plus retention to 7 years for a subset. Is that supported?
[06:09] Maya: Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM or object store; retention is configurable. For Hosted we'll show the export path; for Dedicated/Private you can retain in your infra. We'll include the specifics in the security deck.
[06:23] Lena: Good. Regarding model pinning and rollouts — we want canary to 5% then 25% then full, with automatic rollback on quality regression.
[06:33] Diego: We support canary rollouts and evaluation hooks; Redwood Optimize can run prompt-based evals and trigger alerts on regressions. We'll include an example pipeline.
[06:45] Tom: Operational runbooks — if we pick Private, what's required from our SRE team?
[06:51] Maya: For on-prem Private you'll handle hardware, network, and storage; Redwood provides the control plane package and deployment scripts. For VPC Private, we coordinate peering and managed control plane with minimal infra touch. We'll surface a checklist.
[07:06] Lena: For the bench harness — will you simulate the exact conversation state size? We have long context windows, up to 8k tokens.
[07:15] Diego: We'll parameterize seq length. For the 8k case we'll do a targeted test but expect higher latencies; the runtime's kernel selection matters. We'll profile memory and throughput at 8k.
[07:30] Marcus: Is there any way to do an initial hybrid approach — hosted for low-risk features, private for PHI?
[07:36] Maya: Yes — policy-based routing can split requests by dataset sensitivity. We can route PHI to Private and general queries to Hosted/Dedicated. That adds complexity for data routing and KMS handling but is common.
[07:51] Priya: About keys — we need BYOK (bring your own key) and proof that keys never leave our HSM.
[07:58] Diego: For Dedicated and Private we can integrate with your KMS/HSM; Hosted supports BYOK in many regions — we'll validate the exact flow.
[08:10] Lena: Can we run an initial short-run benchmark just on Hosted while you stand up Dedicated infra? We want a quick baseline.
[08:18] Maya: Yes — we can do Hosted baseline in 1–2 days if you provide traffic samples and authentication. Then once you sign the pilot, we bring up Dedicated instances for parallel tests.
[08:31] Tom: Ok that would be great. On success criteria — product wants: feature parity, p95 under 400ms for chat median profile, degradation < 10% vs internal model, and cost within 15% of current baseline. Security wants SOC2 + KMS + SSO plus log retention.
[08:51] Maya: We'll convert that into measurable gates: run bench, produce report with metrics, and a gating rubric.
[08:58] Diego: For the benchmarks: we'll include raw CSVs, summary dashboards, and a small perf checklist: model latency, p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost/1M tokens, and variance across regions.
[09:12] Lena: Who will run the bench?
[09:15] Diego: We'll run the harness with your data samples but we ask for a small team to review results. We'll provide the scripts and you can re-run if needed.
[09:24] Marcus: About network — if we go Dedicated, do we need peering or can you provide static egress IPs?
[09:30] Maya: We can provide static egress IP ranges for Dedicated; for Hosted we provide region endpoints and optional VPC peering for enterprise accounts.
[09:41] Priya: Any compliance concerns with embeddings? We do not want PII to be stored long-term.
[09:47] Diego: Embeddings can be ephemeral; by default we don't persist customer inputs for training unless you opt in. We'll show data retention settings.
[09:58] Tom: Great. Can we define the 4-week cadences concretely?
[10:03] Maya: Proposed: Week A (Dec 20–24): Security docs + traffic samples exchanged; Hosted baseline run; Week B (Dec 27–31): Benchmark sprint — run three profiles across Hosted and Dedicated (if ready); Week C (Jan 3–7): Pilot on chosen mode with a subset of real traffic; Week D (Jan 10–14): Final validation and decision. We can compress or extend as needed.
[10:32] Lena: Legal will need to review DPA clauses for EU residency. Can you share standard DPA?
[10:37] Maya: Yes — included in the security pack.
[10:40] Priya: On monitoring — we need token-level cost attribution and traceability to user id. Is that supported?
[10:47] Diego: Yes, Redwood Console has token-level cost breakdown and tracing hooks that can include user identifiers (masked if needed).
[10:55] Tom: One more — do you support model quantization inference quality tests? We don't want hallucination increase with 4-bit quant.
[11:03] Diego: We'll measure quality via prompt-based eval suites. We'll run A/B checks across precision variants and include BLEU-like or task-specific metrics depending on your task.
[11:17] Marcus: For Private on-prem: what's the expected ops burden week to week?
[11:22] Maya: If you self-manage, expect ~2 FTE SRE for 24/7 at our scale for maintenance, patching, and capacity. We can offer a managed support contract to share some of that load.
[11:37] Lena: Ok that helps.
[11:39] (multiple speakers) small cross talk and agreement noises
[11:44] Diego: I'll draft a benchmark plan and share by Monday. It'll include the exact request shapes, concurrency patterns, and data requirements.
[11:51] Maya: I'll attach the security pack and DPA. We'll also include a cost model template.
[11:58] Tom: I'll circulate internal acceptance criteria doc to Maya and Lena after the call.
[12:03] Priya: We'll audit the pack and push back with any gaps.
[12:08] Lena: Quick question — if time allows, could you run a mini-latency test now on Hosted?
[12:13] Maya: We can do a quick smoke but we'd need your auth token. Let's skip for today and schedule it after artifacts are shared.
[12:22] Diego: One more note: we'll test cold vs warm KV cache scenarios and show delta for p99.
[12:30] Marcus: That will be useful.
[12:33] Maya: Great — recap of agreements: 1) Maya sends security pack and DPA by 2027-12-09; 2) Verdigris shares traffic samples and baseline costs by 2027-12-08; 3) Diego shares benchmark harness and schedule by 2027-12-13; 4) Aim to run Hosted baseline week of 2027-12-20 and full pilot early Jan.
[12:58] Tom: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[13:01] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up in email and add calendar invites.

End of recording.

References/Links mentioned (notes):

Quality notes: transcript contains speaker label approximations, some technical terms may be mis-transcribed (e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes heard as 'K V cash' or 'Radwood Private' misheard).

Gating rubric (quick sketch):
- Pass if: p95 <= 400ms for chat profile AND cost delta <= +15% vs baseline AND SOC2/KMS/SSO requirements satisfied.
- Conditional if: p95 > 400ms but < 600ms and cost delta within 5% — require mitigation plan and second run.
- Fail if: inability to meet audit/logging/KMS constraints or p99 variance > 2x baseline.

Action items repeated: see action_items metadata above.
